description: Comparative Benchmarks: BEJSON 105 & MFDB v1.40 vs SQL (SQLite)
author: Elton Boehnen

cascading_integrity_metrics.notes: SQLite executes in-process B-tree page deletion; MFDB executes cross-file two-phase snapshot-guarded atomic writes with Parent_Hierarchy validation.

factors.bejson_105: Zero binary dependencies (pure text, universal Python/JS/TS/Shell stdlib)

factors.sqlite: Requires serialization to JSON/SQL text with high token overhead
In-memory / Disk B-tree page traversals (~120k ops/sec)
Single monolithic database file or complex ATTACH DATABASE locks
factors.bejson_105: Discrete federated entity files with bidirectional Parent_Hierarchy

factors.sqlite: Opaque binary file (cannot cleanly git diff / merge)
factors.bejson_105: Deterministic plaintext JSON (clean line-based git diff and merge)
